policy.method_note: Per-corridor volumes are TRANSPARENT DERIVATIONS from sourced throughput x a labelled premium-eligible share, shown as `derived_demand_record` with confidence=derived_pending_validation. Published fares are SOURCED (real operator/list prices), not fabricated. Capture is applied downstream by the cascade (LB-254): Grab is a CONTESTED super-app, not captive -> contested capture band, NOT 0.90.

market_demand_anchors.evidence: Rassada Pier (Phuket) <-> Phi Phi: ~97 weekly sailings; fares from ~$18.
Phi Phi <-> Rassada: ~275-366 crossings per week depending on season (Jun-Sep peak).
Rassada Pier ferries carry up to 590 passengers per vessel; sailing 1h30-2h06.

corridors.premium_ceiling_note: Private speedboat charters Phuket<->Phi Phi list THB 12,000-25,000 per boat (premium transfer ceiling).

inputs.load_factor_basis: Blended annual load factor across high/low season (peak Jun-Sep runs 275-366 crossings/wk; shoulder lower). LABELLED ASSUMPTION.
inputs.premium_share_basis: Share above the THB 600 ferry floor willing to pay for a premium foiling transfer (resort guests, seasickness-averse, time-sensitive). Labelled assumption.

derived_demand_record.calc: 97 sailings/wk * 52 wk * 590 cap * 0.55 LF = ~1.64M corridor seats/yr (gross, both directions implied in schedule). One-way pax pool ~ 818k/yr. Premium-eligible = 818k * 0.12 = ~98,200 premium one-way trips/yr.
derived_demand_record.fare_basis: THB 600 standard ferry = ~$17 contested floor; speedboat THB 700-1,200 and charter ceiling far higher.

corridors.corridor: Phuket (Rassada/Ao Nam Mao) -> Krabi (Klong Jilad) / Ao Nang

fare_baseline_thb.class: Direct speedboat Rassada->Ao Nam Mao/Klong Jilad

demand_anchors.evidence: Daily direct speedboat Rassada Pier -> Ao Nam Mao / Krabi Klong Jilad, 1h45, departs 08:45.

demand_anchors.source: CAAT / Department of Airports (Krabi International Airport, KBV) 2023 final traffic
demand_anchors.evidence: Krabi International Airport handled 2,320,841 passengers in 2023 (+63.6% YoY), 6th-busiest in Thailand. Gateway demand proxy for onward Phuket<->Krabi/Ao Nang island transfers.

inputs.note: Krabi (Klong Jilad) is a major Andaman ferry node feeding Railay/Ao Nang; corridor volume pending Marine Dept / Klong Jilad throughput data.

official_volume_validation.official_anchor: Krabi Int'l Airport 2,320,841 pax (2023, CAAT). Bounds the onward-transfer demand pool feeding the Phuket<->Krabi/Ao Nang marine corridor.
official_volume_validation.operator_correction: Krabi International Airport is operated by the Department of Airports (DOA), NOT AOT. (Chase-list said 'AOT - Krabi'; corrected.) AOT operates Phuket (HKT), which handled 13,977,030 pax in 2023.
official_volume_validation.residual_gap: Klong Jilad Pier (Krabi) registered ferry passenger throughput still pending Krabi Marine Office for the corridor-specific (not gateway) volume.
official_volume_validation.moves_to_measured: Gateway demand now tier-1 official; corridor-specific pier throughput remains the open lock.

corridors.vessel_gate: <=70nm -> N30 Pioneer II (short-hop; N35 Shuttle at scale)

demand_anchors.evidence: Ao Nang<->Railay served by shared longtail cooperative; Railay is road-inaccessible so ALL access is by boat (100% captive water corridor).

inputs.captive_note: Railay has NO road access -> every visitor arrives by boat. This is a structurally captive short-hop; longtail floor THB 100-200. Premium upside is comfort/speed, not access.

official_volume_validation.search_result: No official Ao Nang<->Railay longtail passenger count or Railay Beach visitor figure is published by the cooperative, TAT Krabi, or Marine Dept as of this pass. Only anecdotal press ('hundreds of day-trippers daily').
official_volume_validation.regional_ceiling_context: Krabi Int'l Airport 2,320,841 pax (2023) bounds the province arrival pool from which Railay day-trips draw; Railay is road-inaccessible (fully captive boat access).
official_volume_validation.honest_hold: null beats confidently-wrong: corridor stays derived_pending_validation. Captive geometry means any future TAT Railay visitor figure would be a near-direct boat-volume proxy.
official_volume_validation.moves_to_measured: Pending cooperative manifest or TAT Krabi Railay-specific arrivals.

corridors.corridor: Phang Nga Bay day-tour cluster (Ao Po / Bang Rong -> James Bond Island / Ao Phang Nga NP)
corridors.premium_ceiling_note: Private Phang Nga Bay charters list THB 18,000-35,000 per boat/day.

demand_anchors.source: Ao Phang Nga National Park / AsiaByLocals
demand_anchors.evidence: James Bond Island sits in Ao Phang Nga National Park (400 sq km marine park); one of Phuket's highest-volume day-tour anchors, departing Ao Po / Bang Rong piers.

demand_anchors.source: DNP (Dept of National Parks) via Ao Phang Nga NP record
demand_anchors.evidence: Ao Phang Nga National Park recorded 999,035 visitors in 2019 (DNP official figure). Park includes Khao Phing Kan / 'James Bond Island'.
DNP parks system drew 18.6M visitors FY2024 (+17.7% vs FY2023's 15.8M), confirming strong post-COVID recovery toward 2019 levels.

inputs.note: High-volume day-tour corridor; per-pax tour price from $43. Annual tour volume pending DNP / operator data. Premium charter ceiling THB 18k-35k/boat.

official_volume_validation.official_anchor: Ao Phang Nga National Park 999,035 visitors (2019, DNP). Direct measure of the day-tour visitor pool entering the bay (James Bond Island / Khao Phing Kan).
official_volume_validation.year_caveat: 2019 is the clean pre-COVID measured year; FY2024 system-wide DNP recovery (+17.7%) supports treating ~1.0M as the steady-state day-tour pool ceiling.
official_volume_validation.residual_gap: Ao Po Grand Marina / Bang Rong Pier departure-side throughput (Marine Dept Phuket) would cross-check the per-pier split; park figure already anchors the pool.
official_volume_validation.moves_to_measured: Volume frame upgraded derived -> measured (DNP tier-1).
